records.source: Ὀψὲ δὲ σαββάτων, τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ εἰς μίαν σαββάτων, ἦλθεν Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία θεωρῆσαι τὸν τάφον.
records.gloss: Late then of [the] Sabbaths, at the dawning toward [the] first [day] of [the] week, came Mary the Magdalene and the other Mary to see the tomb.
pieces: The Sabbath was over, and the first day of the week was just beginning to dawn, when Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the tomb.

L.1: Now after [the] Sabbath, as it was dawning toward [the] first [day] of [the] week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the tomb.

R.1: The Sabbath was over. On Sunday morning, as the sky was just getting light, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to look at the tomb.

decisions.choice: after the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The word can mean "late" or, with this case, "after". "Late on the Sabbath" would put the visit on Saturday evening, when the Sabbath ended at sunset; but the next words speak of the dawn of the first day, which fits "after the Sabbath" and the morning of the other Gospels (Mark 16:2).

decisions.choice: as the first day of the week was dawning: early on Sunday morning
alternatives: as the first day was beginning, on Saturday evening
decisions.reason: "The first of the Sabbaths" is a Jewish way of saying the first day of the week, our Sunday. The verb means to grow light; Luke 23:54 uses it of a day beginning at sunset, but here the sense of daybreak is the more natural one.

decisions.choice: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary: the women who watched the burial
decisions.reason: Both sat facing the tomb when Jesus was buried (27:61). The other Mary is the mother of James and Joseph (27:56). Magdalene means she came from Magdala, on the Sea of Galilee.

decisions.choice: Sunday morning; the sky was just getting light
alternatives: the first day of the week was dawning
decisions.reason: Readable names the day and says what "dawning" means.

records.heading: The tomb is empty

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας· ἄγγελος γὰρ κυρίου καταβὰς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ προσελθὼν ἀπεκύλισε τὸν λίθον καὶ ἐκάθητο ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And behold, an earthquake came about great; an angel for of [the] Lord having come down out of heaven and having come to [it] rolled away the stone and was sitting upon it.
pieces: Suddenly the earth shook violently, because an angel of the Lord had come down from heaven. He went to the stone, rolled it back and sat on it.

L.2: And look, a great earthquake took place, for an angel of [the] Lord, coming down out of heaven and approaching, rolled away the stone and was sitting on it.

R.2: Suddenly there was a strong earthquake. An angel of the Lord had come down from heaven. He went to the tomb and rolled the stone away from the entrance. Then he sat on top of it.

decisions.choice: a great earthquake: like the one at Jesus's death
decisions.reason: The earth shook when Jesus died and tombs were opened (27:51-54). Now it shakes again as his own tomb is opened. In Scripture the earth trembles when God comes (Psalm 68:8; 114:7).

decisions.choice: for: the earthquake came with the angel's coming
alternatives: the earthquake caused the stone to move
decisions.reason: The word "for" links the shaking to the angel's coming down. It is the angel, not the earthquake, who rolls the stone away.

decisions.choice: an angel of the Lord: a messenger from God
decisions.reason: As in 1:20 and 2:13, "the Lord" is God, and the angel is his messenger. The same phrase frames the Gospel: an angel of the Lord speaks at Jesus's birth and at his rising.

decisions.choice: rolled away the stone, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: rolled away the stone from the door
rolled away the stone from the door of the tomb
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "from the door", and some add "of the tomb" as well. The SBLGNT has the shorter text. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); suddenly (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: from the entrance
decisions.reason: Readable says where the stone was: across the entrance of the tomb (27:60).

decisions.choice: he, him, his for the angel: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The pronouns in 28:2-4 refer to the angel, not to God or Jesus, so they take no capitalization setting.

records.source: ἦν δὲ ἡ εἰδέα αὐτοῦ ὡς ἀστραπὴ καὶ τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ λευκὸν ὡς χιών.
records.gloss: Was now the appearance of him like lightning and the clothing of him white as snow.
pieces: He looked like a flash of lightning, and his clothing was snow-white.

L.3: And his appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.

R.3: He was as bright as lightning. His clothes were as white as snow.

decisions.choice: appearance: how he looked, above all his face
decisions.reason: The word means what is seen of someone. The brightness of lightning is the point of the comparison.

decisions.choice: like lightning ... white as snow: the look of heavenly beings in Daniel
alternatives: a plain description with no echo
decisions.reason: Daniel sees a figure whose face is like lightning (Daniel 10:6), and the Ancient of Days in clothing white as snow (Daniel 7:9). Jesus's own clothes became white as light at his transfiguration (17:2).

decisions.choice: he looked like a flash of lightning (B); he was as bright as lightning (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the comparison shows: he shone.

records.source: ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ φόβου αὐτοῦ ἐσείσθησαν οἱ τηροῦντες καὶ ἐγενήθησαν ὡς νεκροί.
records.gloss: From now the fear of him were shaken those keeping guard and became as dead [men].
pieces: In terror of him the guards trembled, and they became like dead men.

L.4: And from fear of him those keeping guard were shaken and became like dead [men].

R.4: The soldiers guarding the tomb were so afraid of the angel that they shook. Then they lay as still as dead men.

decisions.choice: were shaken: trembled with fear
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "earthquake" in 28:2. The earth shook, and so did the guards.

decisions.choice: those keeping guard: the soldiers posted at the tomb
decisions.reason: Pilate let the chief priests post a guard and seal the stone so that no one could steal the body (27:62-66).

decisions.choice: became like dead men: fainted or lay motionless
decisions.reason: "Like" makes it a comparison. They are later able to go and report (28:11). The men set to guard a dead man become like the dead themselves.

decisions.choice: of the angel; lay as still as dead men
alternatives: of him; became like dead men
decisions.reason: Readable names the angel and says what "became like dead men" looked like.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν ταῖς γυναιξίν· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε ὑμεῖς, οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ζητεῖτε·
records.gloss: Answering now the angel said to the women, Not fear you, I know for that Jesus the [one] having been crucified you seek;
pieces: But the angel said to the women, "You need not be afraid. I know that you are looking for Jesus, the one who was crucified.

L.5: But the angel answered and said to the women, "You, do not be afraid, for I know that you are seeking Jesus, who has been crucified.

R.5: The angel said to the women, "Do not be afraid. I know you are looking for Jesus, who was put to death on a cross.

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, you women, unlike the guards
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, which Greek does for emphasis. The guards are terrified (28:4), but the women have no reason to fear.

decisions.choice: answered: responded to the scene, not to a question
alternatives: replied to something the women said
decisions.reason: Matthew often uses "answering" to introduce a reply to a situation. The women have said nothing.

decisions.choice: the one who has been crucified: the crucified one
alternatives: the one who was once crucified
decisions.reason: The perfect participle describes Jesus by what was done to him and remains true of him. The risen Jesus is still the one who was crucified.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 28:7
alternatives: closing and reopening at each sentence
decisions.reason: The angel's words run across three sentences (28:5-7), so the quotation marks stay open to the end.

decisions.choice: put to death on a cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what crucifixion was.

records.source: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν· δεῦτε ἴδετε τὸν τόπον ὅπου ἔκειτο·
records.gloss: Not he is here, he was raised for, as he said; come see the place where he was lying;
pieces: He is not here. He has been raised, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} foretold. Come and see where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was lying.

L.6: He is not here, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was raised, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. Come, see the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was lying.

R.6: He is not here. God has raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to life, just as Jesus said would happen. Come and see the place where {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body was lying.

decisions.choice: he was raised: God raised him
alternatives: he rose by his own power
decisions.reason: The verb is passive. Scripture often leaves God unnamed as the one who acts. Matthew uses the same form when Jesus foretells his rising (16:21; 17:23; 20:19).

decisions.choice: as he said: Jesus's own words about his rising
alternatives: a general reference to the prophets
decisions.reason: Jesus said he would be killed and raised on the third day (16:21; 17:23; 20:19), and that after being raised he would go ahead of them to Galilee (26:32).

decisions.choice: where he was lying, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "where the Lord was lying". Several early manuscripts lack "the Lord", and the SBLGNT follows them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: just as he foretold
decisions.reason: Balanced makes clear that Jesus said this beforehand.

decisions.choice: God has raised him back to life; Jesus; his body
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raised him, as the passive implies, names Jesus to keep the two apart, and says that it was his body that had lain there.

records.source: καὶ ταχὺ πορευθεῖσαι εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἰδοὺ προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε· ἰδοὺ εἶπον ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: And quickly having gone say to the disciples of him that He was raised from the dead, and behold he goes before you into Galilee, there him you will see; behold I told you.
pieces: Hurry now, and give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples this message: 'He has been raised from the dead! He is on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way to Galilee ahead of you, and that is where you will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.' That is my message to you."

L.7: And go quickly and tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, 'He was raised from the dead, and look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.' Look, I have told you."

R.7: Go quickly and tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, 'Jesus has been raised from death! He is going to Galilee ahead of you. You will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there.' That is what I came to tell you."

decisions.choice: he is going ahead of you into Galilee: as Jesus promised
decisions.reason: On the night of his arrest Jesus said, "after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee" (26:32). The verb is the one used of a shepherd going before his flock (26:31).

decisions.choice: is going ahead: already on his way
decisions.reason: The present tense speaks of what is already happening. Jesus is on his way to meet them.

decisions.choice: look, I have told you: the angel's message is delivered
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the end of a message: the angel has done what he was sent to do.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered, or carried by the sentence (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: inner quotation marks for the message
alternatives: indirect speech: tell them that he was raised
decisions.reason: The Greek gives the message in the words the women are to say, so it stands in inner quotation marks.

decisions.choice: followers; Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable calls the disciples followers, as in 10:1, and names Jesus in the message.

records.source: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ταχὺ ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου μετὰ φόβου καὶ χαρᾶς μεγάλης ἔδραμον ἀπαγγεῖλαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And having gone out quickly from the tomb with fear and joy great they ran to tell the disciples of him.
pieces: Quickly the women left the tomb. Fear and great joy filled them as they ran to tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

L.8: And going away quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, they ran to tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

R.8: The women left the tomb quickly. They were afraid, but they also felt great joy. They ran to tell Jesus's followers what had happened.

decisions.choice: fear: awe at what God has done, mixed with alarm
decisions.reason: The angel told them not to be afraid (28:5), yet fear remains beside joy. Matthew uses the same word for the awe of people who see God at work (9:8; 17:6).

decisions.choice: great joy: like the joy of the magi
decisions.reason: The magi "rejoiced with very great joy" when they found the child (2:10). The Gospel that began with joy at his birth ends with joy at his rising.

decisions.choice: the women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, which the Greek carries in the verb.

decisions.choice: what had happened; Jesus's followers
decisions.reason: Readable says what they ran to tell and whose followers they were.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἰησοῦς ὑπήντησεν αὐταῖς λέγων· Χαίρετε· αἱ δὲ προσελθοῦσαι ἐκράτησαν αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And behold Jesus met them saying, Greetings; they and having come to [him] took hold of him the feet and worshiped him.
pieces: All at once Jesus stood in their path. "Greetings!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them. They went to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, held on to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and bowed in worship before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.9: And look, Jesus met them, saying, "Greetings!" And coming to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], they took hold of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.9: Suddenly Jesus met them on the way. He said, "Greetings!" The women came close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They held on to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: Greetings: the everyday greeting
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary greeting of the day, used even by Judas (26:49). Its root is the root of "joy", so after 28:8 a reader may also hear in it a call to rejoice; but as a greeting it means simply hello.

decisions.choice: took hold of his feet: a gesture of humble honor
alternatives: a plea to keep him from leaving
decisions.reason: People fell at the feet of someone they honored or begged (2 Kings 4:27). The women touch real feet: the risen Jesus is not a ghost (compare 14:26).

decisions.choice: worshiped: bowed down before him
alternatives: paid him respect as a teacher
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low before someone. Matthew uses it of the magi (2:2, 11) and of the disciples in the boat (14:33), and again in 28:17. Here it is worship of the risen Lord.

decisions.choice: and look, Jesus met them, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: as they were going to tell his disciples, look, Jesus met them
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts begin the verse with "as they were going to tell his disciples". The earliest manuscripts lack it, and the SBLGNT leaves it out. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: look (L); all at once (B); suddenly (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: bowed in worship
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the bodily act the verb describes, as the women are already at his feet.

records.source: τότε λέγει αὐταῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε· ὑπάγετε ἀπαγγείλατε τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου ἵνα ἀπέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, κἀκεῖ με ὄψονται.
records.gloss: Then says to them Jesus, Not fear; go tell the brothers of me that they should go into Galilee, and there me they will see.
pieces: Then Jesus told them, "Have no fear. Go and take word to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers: they are to set out for Galilee, and there they will see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.10: Then Jesus says to them, "Do not be afraid. Go, tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers to go away into Galilee, and there they will see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.10: Jesus told them, "Do not be afraid. Go and tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers to go to Galilee. That is where they will see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: my brothers: the disciples
decisions.reason: In 28:7 the angel spoke of "his disciples", and in 28:16 it is the eleven who go to Galilee. Jesus had called his disciples his brothers before (12:49-50).

decisions.choice: brothers: those who had deserted him are still his family
decisions.reason: The disciples had fled at his arrest (26:56), and Peter had denied him (26:69-75). Jesus still calls them his brothers.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: brothers, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Here the brothers are a particular group, the eleven men who go to Galilee (28:16), so the word stays "brothers". Where Jesus speaks of believers in general (12:50; 23:8), the inclusive wording applies.

records.source: Πορευομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἰδού τινες τῆς κουστωδίας ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν ἅπαντα τὰ γενόμενα.
records.gloss: [As] were going now they behold some of the guard having come into the city reported to the chief priests all the things having happened.
pieces: The women were still on their way when some of the soldiers from the guard came into the city and gave the chief priests a full report of what had happened.

L.11: And as they were going, look, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests all the things that had happened.

R.11: While the women were still going, some of the soldiers who had guarded the tomb went into the city. They told the leading priests everything that had happened.

decisions.choice: the guard: the soldiers posted at the tomb
decisions.reason: The word is a Latin loanword for a guard of soldiers. Pilate told the chief priests, "You have a guard" (27:65); the guards here report to the priests and fear the governor (28:14), so they may have been Roman soldiers put at the priests' disposal, or the temple's own guard.

decisions.choice: as they were going: while the women were on their way
decisions.reason: "They" are the women of 28:8-10. Matthew sets the two reports side by side: the women go to the disciples, the guards to the chief priests.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the women so that "they" is not taken as the guards.

decisions.choice: leading priests
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase, as in 2:4.

records.heading: The guards' story

records.source: καὶ συναχθέντες μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων συμβούλιόν τε λαβόντες ἀργύρια ἱκανὰ ἔδωκαν τοῖς στρατιώταις λέγοντες· Εἴπατε ὅτι Οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς ἐλθόντες ἔκλεψαν αὐτὸν ἡμῶν κοιμωμένων·
records.gloss: And having been gathered together with the elders counsel then having taken silver pieces many they gave to the soldiers \v 13 saying, Say that The disciples of him by night having come stole him, we being asleep;
pieces: After meeting with the elders and deciding what to do, the chief priests paid the soldiers a large sum of money
and gave them their story: "Tell people, 'His disciples came in the night while we were asleep and stole {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away.'

L.12: And having gathered with the elders and taken counsel, they gave a large sum of silver coins to the soldiers,
L.13: saying, "Say, 'His disciples came by night and stole {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} while we were sleeping.'

R.12: The leading priests met with the elders and made a plan. They paid the soldiers a lot of money.
R.13: They said to the soldiers, "Say this: 'His followers came at night and stole {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body while we were sleeping.'

decisions.choice: the elders: leaders of the people who sat on the council with the chief priests
decisions.reason: The chief priests and elders had planned Jesus's arrest and handed him to Pilate (26:3-4; 27:1-2).

decisions.choice: silver coins in plenty: a large sum of money
decisions.reason: The word means pieces of silver, that is, money. Matthew used it of the thirty pieces of silver paid to Judas (26:15; 27:3-10). Those who paid for Jesus's betrayal now pay to hide his rising.

decisions.choice: his disciples stole him: the very story the priests had feared
decisions.reason: The priests asked for the guard so that the disciples could not steal the body and say he had been raised (27:64). Now they tell the guards to say that this happened.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 28:14
decisions.reason: The priests' words run on into the next sentence, so the quotation marks stay open to its end. The story they give the soldiers stands in inner quotation marks.

decisions.choice: his body; made a plan; a lot of money
decisions.reason: Readable says that it was his body they claimed was stolen, and uses plain words for the plan and the money.

records.source: καὶ ἐὰν ἀκουσθῇ τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος, ἡμεῖς πείσομεν αὐτὸν καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους ποιήσομεν.
records.gloss: And if is heard this before the governor, we will persuade [him] and you free of care will make.
pieces: If the governor hears about this, we will win him over and see that you have nothing to worry about."

L.14: And if this is heard before the governor, we will persuade him and make you free of worry."

R.14: If the governor hears about this, we will talk to him. We will make sure you do not get into trouble."

decisions.choice: heard before the governor: reaches the governor's ears
alternatives: is heard as a case in the governor's court
decisions.reason: The words can mean that the report comes to the governor, or that the matter comes before him for judgment. Either way the priests promise to protect the soldiers.

decisions.choice: the governor: Pilate
decisions.reason: Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea (27:2). Soldiers who slept on guard and lost their charge could be severely punished.

decisions.choice: persuade: talk him round, perhaps with money
decisions.reason: The verb means to persuade or win over. Matthew does not say how; the priests have just used money with the soldiers.

decisions.choice: him for the governor, with no span
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to Pilate.

records.source: οἱ δὲ λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια ἐποίησαν ὡς ἐδιδάχθησαν.
records.gloss: They and having taken the silver pieces did as they were taught.
pieces: The soldiers took the money and followed their instructions.

L.15: And they took the silver coins and did as they had been instructed.

R.15: The soldiers took the money and said what they had been told to say.

decisions.choice: were instructed: were taught what to say
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual word for teaching. The soldiers are taught a false story; at the end of the chapter Jesus sends his disciples to teach what he commanded (28:20).

decisions.choice: the soldiers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

decisions.choice: said what they had been told to say
decisions.reason: Readable says what they did: they told the story they were given.

records.source: Καὶ διεφημίσθη ὁ λόγος οὗτος παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις μέχρι τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
records.gloss: And was spread abroad the word this among Jews until the today day.
pieces: And this is the account that has gone around among Jews up to the present day.

L.15: And this account was spread about among Jews until the present day.

R.15: Even now, this story is still being told among Jewish people.

decisions.choice: until the present day: up to the time Matthew wrote
decisions.reason: "To this day" is the writer's time, as in 27:8. Matthew tells his first readers where a story they may have heard came from.

decisions.choice: among Jews: in Jewish circles, not all Jewish people
alternatives: among the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: The noun has no article. Matthew, a Jewish writer, does not say that all Jews believed the story, only that it was told among Jews. The chief priests' story is the issue here, not the Jewish people.

decisions.choice: even now
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the writer's "now"; the meaning note says whose time it is.

records.source: Οἱ δὲ ἕνδεκα μαθηταὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς τὸ ὄρος οὗ ἐτάξατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν προσεκύνησαν, οἱ δὲ ἐδίστασαν.
records.gloss: The and eleven disciples went into Galilee to the mountain where had appointed them Jesus, \v 17 and having seen him they worshiped, some but doubted.
pieces: The eleven disciples made their way to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had appointed for them.
When they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there, they bowed in worship, but some had doubts.

L.16: And the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them,
L.17: and seeing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they worshiped, but some doubted.

R.16: Then the eleven followers went to Galilee. They went to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go.
R.17: When they saw Jesus, they worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But some of them were not sure what to think.

decisions.choice: the eleven: the Twelve without Judas
decisions.reason: Judas had betrayed Jesus and hanged himself (27:3-5).

decisions.choice: the mountain Jesus had appointed: a place he had named to them
decisions.reason: The verb means to arrange or appoint. Matthew has not told us when Jesus named the place, and he does not name the mountain. In Matthew mountains are places where Jesus teaches and is revealed (5:1; 17:1).

decisions.choice: some doubted: some of the eleven hesitated
alternatives: they all worshiped, though they doubted
decisions.reason: The words can mean that some of the eleven doubted, that all of them worshiped and yet wavered, or that others there doubted. The verb means to waver or hesitate, as of Peter on the water (14:31); it is not refusal to believe. Matthew does not explain it, and Jesus comes to them all (28:18).

decisions.choice: worshiped: bowed down before him
decisions.reason: As in 28:9, the women's response is now the disciples' (compare 14:33).

decisions.choice: had doubts
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a phrase that leaves room for wavering rather than unbelief.

decisions.choice: some of them were not sure what to think
decisions.reason: Readable takes "some" as some of the eleven, the reading the meaning note gives first, and says what wavering is.

records.heading: Sent to all the nations

records.source: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἐδόθη μοι πᾶσα ἐξουσία ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς·
records.gloss: And having come to [them] Jesus spoke to them saying, Was given to me all authority in heaven and on the earth;
pieces: Jesus came up to them and said, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been placed in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands.

L.18: And coming to [them], Jesus spoke to them, saying, "All authority in heaven and on earth was given to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.18: Jesus came to them and said, "God has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all authority in heaven and on earth.

decisions.choice: all authority was given to me: Daniel 7:14
alternatives: a general statement with no echo
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7:13-14 one like a son of man comes before God and is given authority, and all the nations serve him. The Greek Old Testament uses the same words "authority was given". Jesus, the Son of Man, now claims that authority without limit.

decisions.choice: was given: given by God the Father
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, with God as the giver, as in 11:27: "All things have been handed over to me by my Father."

decisions.choice: all authority in heaven and on earth: rule over all things
decisions.reason: Jesus had authority on earth to forgive sins (9:6). Now it is all authority, in heaven as well. The devil offered him the kingdoms of the world for worship (4:8-9); the Father has given him more.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 28:20
decisions.reason: Jesus's last words run across two sentences, so the quotation marks stay open to the end of the Gospel.

decisions.choice: has been placed in my hands
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a natural English picture of being entrusted with something.

decisions.choice: God has given
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver, as the passive implies.

records.source: πορευθέντες οὖν μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, διδάσκοντες αὐτοὺς τηρεῖν πάντα ὅσα ἐνετειλάμην ὑμῖν· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.
records.gloss: Having gone therefore make disciples all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, \v 20 teaching them to keep all things as many as I commanded you; and behold I with you am all the days until the completion of the age.
pieces: Go, then, and make disciples of all the nations: baptize them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
and teach them to keep everything I have commanded you. And remember this: I myself am with you every day, until the close of the age."

L.19: Going, therefore, make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
L.20: teaching them to keep all things that I commanded you; and look, I am with you all the days until the completion of the age."

R.19: So go and make disciples of people from every nation. Baptize them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
R.20: Teach them to do all that I have told you to do. And remember, I am with you every day, until the end of this age."

decisions.choice: all the nations: all peoples, Israel among them
decisions.reason: The word can mean "the nations" in general or "the Gentiles" as distinct from Israel. Before, Jesus sent the Twelve only to Israel (10:5-6; 15:24). Now the limit is lifted: the good news is for every people, as in 24:14 and 25:32, where "all the nations" stand before the Son of Man. Some read the word here as the Gentiles alone.

decisions.choice: into the name: into belonging to the one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: "Name" is singular for all three. To be baptized into someone's name is to be brought under that one's ownership and care. This is the only place in Matthew where the Father, the Son and the Spirit are named together; at Jesus's baptism all three were present (3:16-17).

decisions.choice: I am with you: the promise of Immanuel, God with us
alternatives: a promise of the disciples' memory of him
decisions.reason: Matthew began with the name Immanuel, "God with us" (1:23); he ends with Jesus's promise, "I am with you." God gave the same promise to Moses, Joshua and Israel (Exodus 3:12; Joshua 1:5; Haggai 1:13). The completion of the age is the end of this world's time, when the Son of Man comes (13:39-40, 49; 24:3).

decisions.choice: the end of the Gospel, without "Amen"
alternatives: the completion of the age. Amen.
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts end the Gospel with "Amen". Several of the earliest lack it, and the SBLGNT leaves it out. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Going (L); Go ... baptize ... teach (B, R)
decisions.reason: The first participle shares the force of the command, so Balanced and Readable say "go". "Baptizing" and "teaching" say how disciples are made; Balanced keeps them under the command with a colon, and Readable gives them as short commands.

decisions.choice: And remember this: I myself am with you (B); And remember, I am with you (R)
alternatives: and look, I am with you
decisions.reason: The word for "look" calls the hearers to attend to the promise. The pronoun "I" is written out for emphasis, which Balanced brings out with "myself".

decisions.choice: keep
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep or guard, as one keeps commandments (19:17). "Keep" holds both doing and holding on to what Jesus commanded.

decisions.choice: people from every nation; in the name
alternatives: all the nations; into the name
decisions.reason: Readable says that the disciples are made from among the people of the nations, as "them" shows, and uses the familiar "in the name"; the meaning note explains "into".
